AISEE-BIN gives blind and low-vision visitors spoken directions through the Flower Dome, on a phone or AiSee glasses.
Scan the place once. Add the route and stops in our web editor. Then the phone or glasses work out where they are, and guide the visitor.
We're testing two ways to scan: our own app, using the iPhone's ARKit, or Immersal, whose maps also work with the glasses.
In the web editor, anyone on the team can draw walkways, add stops and hazards, and write what the app says.
On October first, we tested the route. Inside the dome, the phone guided us, turn by turn, to Points one, two and three.
The entrance was harder. Our phone scan struggled there, but an Immersal scan found the position straight away.
What's next: one Immersal scan of the whole route, Immersal and ARKit working together, and testing the glasses on site.
